edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: adults in primary or secondary prevention cohorts
edges.mechanism: High Lp(a) adds an inherited apoB-containing particle with pro-atherogenic and pro-thrombotic features, supporting its link to cardiovascular events.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2026 He meta analysis in Clin Cardiol already points to high lipoprotein(a) tracks with higher risk or worse outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.
